decisions.H266_note: written as 'real gain exceeds permuted gain in every pool'; it held in one_unseen and failed only in the underpowered both_unseen

limits: Permutation preserves the marginal pathway distribution but destroys the drug-pathway pairing, which is the intended cut.
Only two pools were run; an opposite result would require all three.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI.

what_the_data_actually_says.permutation_destroys_the_gain: permuted minus identity is +1.50 [-0.21,+3.21] in one_unseen and -0.14 [-1.14,+0.93] in both_unseen, i.e. no gain, exactly as a clean feature should behave
what_the_data_actually_says.real_mapping_matters_where_power_exists: in one_unseen the real gain exceeds the permuted gain by +2.36 pp [+0.29,+4.43]
what_the_data_actually_says.where_it_is_merely_directional: in both_unseen the same contrast is +1.57 pp [-0.14,+3.64]; the direction is right but the pool holds only about 1,830 keys

promotion_status.reason: the pre-registered gate was not met in full, and the cross-dataset check is still outstanding
promotion_status.what_is_cleared: the specific leak hypothesis - that feature count or some structural artefact drives the gain - is not supported, because permuting the mapping removes the gain entirely
promotion_status.what_is_not_cleared: higher power in both_unseen, and replication on a second dataset
